member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.ManuallyApprovesFollowersExtensionName
member.summary: The ActivityPub actor property manuallyApprovesFollowers: when true on a local actor, an inbound follow is not auto-accepted — the actor (operator) must respond with an explicit Accept or Reject. The library's Actor type does not model this property, so it is carried in the actor's (seeded by the host) and echoed onto the public actor document (Resolved Decision #46).

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.ManuallyApprovesMembersExtensionName
member.summary: The ActivityPub group extension property manuallyApprovesMembers: when true on a local community (group), an inbound Join activity from a remote actor is not auto-granted — the operator must respond with an explicit Accept or Reject. Carried in the group's (seeded by the host) and echoed onto the public group document. Communities without the flag retain the legacy auto-grant behavior.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.CapabilitiesTerm
member.summary: The iris:capabilities extension property name (Resolved Decision #11). The full IRI is {NamespaceIri}capabilities; this is the local term. Aliased from the canonical Iris.Core constant () so the server's render path and the client's readers share one source of truth.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.SettingsTerm
member.summary: The iris:settings extension property name: the IRI of the actor/community's settings surface (the AP-native settings change endpoint — an Add/Remove of the actor's own document carrying a settings flag, published to the outbox). When present, a remote client can discover the settings surface from the actor document alone (no hardcoded endpoint paths). The full IRI is {NamespaceIri}settings. Aliased from the canonical Iris.Core constant ().

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.DefaultCapabilitiesNamespaceIri
member.summary: The canonical default iris: namespace base IRI (Resolved Decision #9; Open Question #1 resolved) used when a deployment does not override . The base is configurable per-deployment; this is the out-of-the-box default. This is the single source of truth for the default namespace — Iris.Client aliases it as IrisDocumentExtensions.DefaultNamespaceIri, so a client reading a document from a default-namespace deployment never needs to know the string.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.CapabilitySettings
member.summary: The capability value advertised for the actor/community's settings surface: the AP-native settings change endpoint (an Add/Remove of the actor's own document carrying a settings flag, published to the outbox). When present in iris:capabilities, the actor document also carries an iris:settings extension property whose value is the settings IRI (the outbox IRI, where the settings activities are published). member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.CapabilityLikes

Like/shares are not core ActivityStreams Object collections (the only core one is replies), so this is an Iris-namespaced extension collection; a client discovers it via this capability value and reads the count from the collection's totalItems.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.CapabilityShares
member.summary: The capability value advertised for the per-object shares collection (GET {object}/shares, decision 056 (d)): the actors that announced (boosted) an object, read from the announce reverse index. An Iris-namespaced extension collection, exactly like ; a client reads the boost count from the collection's totalItems.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.ProxyRouteSegment
member.summary: The route segment for the proxy endpoint (the POST /ap/v1/proxy/{target} proxy fallback, Phase 6). Mapped as {RoutePrefix}/proxy/{target} — i.e. the proxy lives under the versioned prefix, like every other endpoint (Resolved Decision #10).

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.DefaultProxyMaxRequestsPerMinute
member.summary: The default per-actor rate limit for the proxy endpoint (requests per minute) when does not override it.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.DefaultAnonymousProxyMaxRequestsPerMinute
member.summary: The default per-client-IP rate limit for the anonymous proxy seam (GET /ap/v1/proxy/{target}, a signed-out visitor's public remote reads) when does not override it. The anonymous seam has no actor identity, so the bound is keyed on the client IP and set far below the per-actor limit (a signed-out browser page load issues a handful of avatar/profile reads, not hundreds of signed federation requests).

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.HealthRouteSegment
member.summary: The route segment for the health-check endpoint (the GET /ap/v1/health observability endpoint, Phase 17). Mapped as {RoutePrefix}/health — i.e. the health endpoint lives under the versioned prefix, like every other endpoint (Resolved Decision #10).

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.ReadyRouteSegment
member.summary: The route segment for the readiness probe (the GET /ap/v1/ready endpoint, Phase 30.2). Mapped as {RoutePrefix}/ready — under the versioned prefix, like the health endpoint. It reports whether the instance has finished loading its signing key material and started its delivery worker: 200 {"ready": true} when ready, 503 {"ready": false} otherwise. A load balancer / orchestrator gates traffic on this (readiness) rather than the liveness /health endpoint, so requests are not routed to an instance that has not yet loaded its keys.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.NamespaceRouteSegment
member.summary: The route segment for the iris: extension namespace document (the GET /ns endpoint, Phase 31.8). Mapped as {NamespaceIri-without-#} — i.e. the JSON-LD context the document declares as @vocab is hosted at the namespace base, so it is resolvable. The namespace base defaults to {BaseUri}/ns#, so the document is served at {BaseUri}/ns.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.DeadLetterRouteSegment
member.summary: The route segment for the outbound-delivery dead-letter queue (the GET /ap/v1/dead-letters endpoint, Phase 83.3). Mapped as {RoutePrefix}/dead-letters — under the versioned prefix, like the health endpoint. It exposes the dead-lettered outbound deliveries (those that exhausted their retry budget) so an operator can inspect them: the count + a bounded peek of the most recent entries (inbox IRI, activity IRI, failure kind, failure detail, attempt count, dead-lettered-at). Read-only (it does not re-drive deliveries; re-driving is an explicit operator action). No authentication: an operator's monitoring scrape reaches it without a signature.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerConstants.DiagnosticsRouteSegment
member.summary: The route segment for the cache-metrics diagnostics endpoint (the GET /ap/v1/diagnostics/caches endpoint, Phase 116.6). Mapped as {RoutePrefix}/diagnostics/caches — under the versioned prefix, like the health endpoint. It reports per-cache hit/miss/stale counters and entry counts so an operator can verify caching is effective. No authentication: an operator's monitoring scrape reaches it without a signature, like the health endpoint.

member.summary:
The instance-actor document at the instance root (GET /, 138.4). A remote platform (notably Lemmy) dereferences the site actor from the instance's root URL before resolving any object on the instance; when the root served only the SPA shell (HTML), that dereference failed and every remote→local resolve was blocked. This handler content-negotiates: when the request is an ActivityPub client (its Accept header names an ActivityStreams or JSON-LD media type), it serves the configured instance actor's public document (the same document serves at /ap/v1/u/{handle}), so the site-actor dereference succeeds. For any other request — a browser navigating to the home page, a curl with no Accept — it returns so the host app's SPA fallback (mapped after the ActivityPub endpoints) serves the shell.
Only the public form is ever served here (never the owner-only privateKey extension): the instance root is a public discovery URL and the owner-only extension requires the request to be authenticated for the instance actor specifically, which a bare root GET is not. A host that wants the authenticated form still uses /ap/v1/u/{handle}.
member.param: The HTTP context (negotiates the content type and cache control).
The persistence provider (the actor store holding the instance actor).
The ActivityPub options (the and base URI used to locate and render the instance actor's document).
The local actor document cache (the public document is served through it, exactly as does, so the root and the versioned route share one cached rendering).
The cancellation token.
member.returns: The instance actor's public document (serialized) when the request is an ActivityPub client and the instance actor exists; when the request is not an ActivityPub client (so the SPA fallback serves the shell) or the instance actor is unconfigured/absent.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.WantsActivityStreams(Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext)
member.summary: Whether the request is an ActivityPub client: its Accept header names an ActivityStreams or JSON-LD media type (application/activity+json, application/ld+json, or a wildcard such as application/*). Used by to content-negotiate the instance-actor document at the root against the SPA shell.
member.param: The HTTP context (reads the Accept header).
member.returns: true when the Accept header signals an ActivityPub/JSON-LD client; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.ActorByIriHandler(Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext,Iris.Server.Stores.IPersistenceProvider,Microsoft.Extensions.Options.IOptions{Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptions},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
The cached-actor-by-IRI endpoint (GET /ap/v1/actor?iri={absolute-actor-iri}, 134.1). Serves the actor document the instance has stored in its database — a local actor or a remote actor the instance cached during federation (the RemoteActorPersister persists a remote actor's document on first encounter). The document is served as-is (the stored document, with its original IRI, name, summary, icon, image, and publicKey) — no live cross-instance fetch, and no Iris-local collection extensions are added (those are only valid for local actors, whose documents are built by ).
This is the "serve known content" half of the directory's "All known" scope: the client consults it first for a known actor's profile, so a cached actor renders even when its home instance is unreachable or the account has been deactivated (a live fetch would 410). When the instance has never cached the actor (an unknown IRI), the endpoint 404s and the client falls back to a live fetch (the proxy).
The response is cacheable for a short window (): the cached document is only refreshed when the instance re-fetches the actor (key resolution / a federated Update), so a modest max-age avoids hammering the store while staying fresh enough for a profile read.
member.param: The HTTP context (reads the ?iri query value; negotiates the content type).
The persistence provider (the actor store and community store to look the stored document up in).
The server options (the instance base URI, used to reject a remote IRI — this endpoint serves local actors / communities only).
The cancellation token.
member.returns: The cached actor or community document (the stored document, serialized) when the instance has it; when the actor is unknown to the instance or ?iri is missing/malformed.

member.summary:
The proxy-fallback endpoint (POST /ap/v1/proxy/{target}, Phase 6). An authenticated actor's browser cannot reach a cross-origin remote instance directly (CORS, and the browser cannot produce an ActivityPub HTTP signature), so it posts the request it wants to make to its own instance's proxy. The endpoint: (1) identifies the actor from the request's Basic auth (), (2) checks the target against the (allowlist + rate limit), and (3) signs and forwards the request to the target with the actor's own key (the per-actor X-Iris-Actor override, Resolved Decision #29), relaying the remote response's status and body back.
The proxied request is a GET to the target: the proxy signs it with the actor's key (the remote instance validates the signature by the actor's document) and copies the client's Accept header. The client's Authorization is not forwarded — the remote authenticates by the HTTP signature, not Basic auth. The target is the {target} catch-all route value (an absolute IRI); the path is passed through as-is so the forwarded request's (request-target) component (the escaped path the signs) is exactly the target's path.
The anonymous seam (GET /ap/v1/proxy/{target}, S2/S14): a SIGNED-OUT visitor's browser also cannot reach a cross-origin remote instance directly (a direct GET is CORS- or CSP-blocked — the signed-out home feed's remote avatars and the signed-out remote actor-detail page were broken by exactly this), so when ProxySettings.AllowAnonymousReads is enabled a cookie-less GET to the proxy is allowed: it is relayed ONLY as an unsigned GET read (writes still require an authenticated actor), the target is checked against the same allowlist policy, and the read is bounded by a per-client-IP rate limit ( — the anonymous seam has no actor identity). A non-anonymous GET (a site cookie is present but not valid for the proxy) still 401s, and an anonymous write (POST without credentials) still 401s.

member.name: F:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.ProxyCacheFreshnessTtl
member.summary: The cache-first freshness window for the proxy endpoint's cached reads (Phase 138): a cached remote actor / community / object whose iris:fetchedAt mark is within this window is served from the local store without a live cross-instance fetch; an older (or unmarked) copy is re-fetched and refreshed. 10 minutes balances profile / object-read latency (no round-trip to the remote for a just-read document) against staleness (a profile edit lands within the window). Mirrors the client's UiContext actor TTL (5 minutes) at a coarser grain — the client's in-memory cache already absorbs the sub-10-minute repeats.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.IsLocalIri(Iris.Core.Identity.Iri,System.Nullable{Iris.Core.Identity.Iri})
member.summary: Whether an IRI is a LOCAL document on this instance (its origin matches the instance's base URI, ignoring trailing slashes and case). Used by the cache-first read (only remote targets are cached — local reads dial directly) and by the local-only cached-actor endpoint (a remote IRI 404s there). Returns when the instance base is unset or the IRI has no origin (a relative / malformed IRI is treated as remote so the caller's safe default applies).
member.param: The IRI to test.
The instance's base URI (e.g. https://a.domain.local), or null.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.TryServeCachedTargetAsync(Iris.Core.Identity.Iri,Iris.Server.Stores.IPersistenceProvider,Iris.Server.Security.RemoteActorPersister,Iris.Server.Security.RemoteCommunityPersister)
member.summary:
The proxy endpoint's cache-first read (Phase 138): for a REMOTE (cross-origin) target, look the target up in the local stores — the actor store (a cached remote person / organization), the community store (a cached remote Group), and the object store (a cached content object) — and decide whether a fresh cached copy can be served without a live fetch.
A FRESH copy (its server-internal iris:fetchedAt mark within ; a Tombstone is always fresh — a deleted remote object is final) is deep-copied (the iris:fetchedAt server-internal field stripped) and returned as a result to serve. A STALE or UNMARKED copy (and an unknown target) yields a lookup whose is null: the caller falls through to a live fetch and, when the cached document is the target's own actor / community, threads it to the refresh path so the fetch overwrites it and stamps it fresh.
Actor / community IRIs are checked before the object store (a Group is an Actor and a cached community is also stored as an object in some flows — the actor / community stores are the authoritative home for those documents). A target that is not an actor, community, or stored object (an unknown IRI, or an activity IRI the object store does not hold) yields null — the caller live-fetches it.
member.param: The remote target IRI to look up.
The persistence provider (actor, community, and object stores).
The remote-actor persister (unused by the lookup itself; kept for symmetry with the refresh path — the lookup only reads).
The remote-community persister (unused by the lookup itself; kept for symmetry with the refresh path).
member.returns: The lookup outcome, or when the target is not a cached actor / community / object (the caller live-fetches).

A document with no mark (persisted before the freshness field existed, or a local / inbound-persisted document) is treated as STALE so the first proxy read refreshes it (and stamps it) — safe, at the cost of one live fetch.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.IsLocallyAuthoredObject(KristofferStrube.ActivityStreams.IObject,System.Nullable{Iris.Core.Identity.Iri})
member.summary: 132.1 — whether a proxied (fetched) object is locally authored (its attributedTo is a local actor on this instance). A locally-authored object's interactions are already recorded by this instance's own handlers (the / / ), so the proxy does not re-walk its remote collections (the object is not really remote — it is a local object being read back through the proxy, e.g. the client's outbox fallback). Returns when the object has no attributedTo or its author is not a local actor (a genuinely remote object, which is the case the interaction sync targets).

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.SyncProxiedObjectInteractionsAsync(Iris.Client.IActivityPubClient,Iris.Server.Stores.IPersistenceProvider,Iris.Core.Identity.Iri,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: 132.1 — syncs the interaction counts of a proxied (remote) object into the local stores. After the proxy stores a remote object (75.3), this walks the remote object's /likes, /shares, and /replies collections (via the proxy's signed , the same transport the proxy used to fetch the object) and records each discovered liker / announcer / reply as an edge in the local / / . The object-document endpoint then derives the object's iris:likedCount / iris:sharedCount / iris:repliedCount from those reverse indexes, so a subsequent local read of the object shows the object's real interaction counts instead of 0.
member.remarks:
Known-edges fallback. When a collection cannot be walked (the remote does not serve it — a non-Iris / strict ActivityStreams instance that does not expose the bare likes / shares extension collections — or is slow / unreachable), the walk yields nothing and the object is simply served with the counts of the interactions this instance has already recorded (from inbound Like / Announce / Reply activities, which the handlers record for stored objects). There is no additional signal to mine; the fallback is "serve what we know."
Bounded and best-effort. Each collection walk is capped (the client's GetLikesAsync / GetSharesAsync / GetRepliesAsync with a 100-item limit — a like/boost/reply set is small and bounded), and any failure (a network error, a 404, a timeout) is swallowed: the proxy relay and the object store are never broken by a failed interaction sync. The walk is best-effort enrichment, not a correctness dependency.
member.param: The proxy's signed (the outbound federation transport; the same client the proxy used to fetch the object).
The local persistence provider (provides the like / announce / reply stores the discovered edges are recorded in).
The IRI of the proxied object whose interactions are being synced.
A cancellation token.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.ForEachCollectionItemAsync(Iris.Client.IActivityPubClient,Iris.Core.Identity.Iri,System.Int32,System.Func{Iris.Core.Identity.Iri,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Threading.Tasks.Task},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: 132.1 — walks a remote collection (via the proxy's signed ) up to a bounded number of items, resolving each item's IRI and invoking with it. Best-effort: any failure (a non-success status, a missing collection, a timeout, a non-IRI item) is swallowed, and the walk simply yields nothing for that collection — the caller's known-edges fallback (serve the counts of already-recorded interactions) then applies. A successful walk of an empty collection yields nothing too (an object with no likes/boosts/replies has empty collections).
member.param: The signed client that walks the collection.
The collection IRI to walk (e.g. {object}/likes).
The maximum number of items to walk (bounds the remote load).
The callback invoked with each item's resolved IRI (null items are skipped).
A cancellation token.

member.summary: Records (or removes) a local mute (F-07). The requesting actor is identified by Basic auth (IActorCredentialValidator); the muted actor is the {target} catch-all route value (an absolute IRI); ?unmute=true removes the mute instead of recording it.
member.remarks: A mute is Iris-specific (there is no ActivityStreams Mute type) and is a local moderation decision: a local actor hides a follow's content from its feed without severing the follow. It is therefore recorded from an authenticated local request — it is not interpreted from a federated activity (which the inbox endpoint would reject, the ActivityStreams library deserializing an unknown type to a generic Object rather than an Activity). The handler: (1) authenticates the actor, (2) resolves the target IRI, and (3) records or removes the mute edge in the moderation store (an un-mute is signalled by ?unmute=true). The response is 204 on success.

Shared inbox: handles POST /ap/v1/shared-inbox — the instance-wide catch-all inbox advertised in every actor document's endpoints.sharedInbox. A remote sender that prefers the shared inbox (e.g. Mastodon, which coalesces delivery targets by preferred_inbox_url) delivers every activity here instead of to a per-actor inbox. The handler verifies the signature (or Bearer token), buffers + parses the body to learn the intended recipient, resolves that recipient (the activity's object for a Follow/Accept/Undo, the embedded object's author for a Create/Announce), and routes the delivery through the same pipeline as a per-actor inbox POST. Before this route existed, the advertised sharedInbox fell through to the catch-all, which returned 200 and silently dropped the body — so a local follower of a shared-inbox-preferring sender never received that sender's posts.
member.remarks: The body is parsed here (before the route is known) because the recipient is not in the URL — it must be read from the activity. The body is then handed back to , which re-buffers (idempotent) and processes the delivery for the resolved recipient, reusing the per-actor rate limit, the activity handlers, and the 202 contract. A delivery whose recipient cannot be resolved (or is not a local actor) is answered 202 and dropped (the activity is not this instance's concern) rather than 4xx — a 4xx would make the sender retry a delivery this instance can never process.

member.summary: Outbox publish: handles POST /ap/v1/u/{handle}/outbox — the write surface for the activities the local actor authors. Per the delivery model, a client never addresses a recipient's inbox for an activity it authors; it publishes the activity to the acting actor's own outbox. This handler signature-validates the acting local actor, records the activity in that actor's outbox (so the actor's feed / outbox collection surfaces it) and the activity store (for resolution and for the remote side to look it up), records the local edge the activity implies (a follow/block/flag/like, or its undo), and — the server's job, not the client's — resolves the recipient and server-delivers the activity to the recipient's inbox.
member.remarks: The recipient is derived from the activity: the activity's object for a // (the actor being followed/blocked/ flagged), the original activity's object for an of one, the object's attributedTo for a (the object's owner), and the author's remote followers for a (the post's federation target). A local-only recipient (a local actor) needs no cross-instance hop — the local edge is already recorded — so the server delivers only to remote recipients (the mirror of 's remote-follower loop).

member.summary: The WRITE SURFACE for the activities a local community (a actor) AUTHORS: a (the community follows a remote actor/community — gap G-3) or an of such a follow (an un-follow). Mirrors for a Group: the client publishes the community-authored activity to the community's own outbox, the server records the activity in the community's outbox (so the community's following collection surfaces the edge) + the activity store, records the community's follows-set edge (the inverse of 's community branch), and is the only thing that delivers the activity to the target's inbox (the server→server hop, signed as the community — a Group signs just like a Person). Requires a valid HTTP signature from the community (validated by SignatureValidationMiddleware); unsigned or invalidly-signed requests are rejected with 401.
member.remarks: Follow vs. Undo. A Follow records the community's follows-set edge () and server-delivers the follow to the target's inbox (signed as the community). An Undo of a follow resolves the original follow from the activity store (the community stored it when it authored it), removes the community's follows-set edge (the inverse of the follow), and server-delivers the Undo to the target's inbox (so the target removes the edge it recorded on receipt). A Follow of a local target records the local edge but performs no cross-instance hop (the local edge is already recorded; the local target is not re-delivered to, matching OutboxPublishHandler's local-recipient rule).

The community's handle (the {name} route value).
The persistence provider (activity store + community store).
The delivery service (schedules the server→server delivery hop).
The id minter (decision 055: mints the community-authored activity's id).

The local collection-page response cache (invalidated on the outbox write so the community's outbox card reflects the new activity immediately).
The degraded-mode gate (Phase 83.4): when degraded (read-only), the write is refused with before touching the store.
The cancellation token.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.ResolveObjectAuthorForDeliveryAsync(Iris.Server.Stores.IPersistenceProvider,Iris.Client.IActivityPubClient,Iris.Core.Identity.Iri,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Resolves the attributedTo owner (author) of the object at for cross-instance delivery: a local object's owner is read from the object store; a remote object's owner is resolved by fetching the object's document over the wire. Used by two outbound paths:
Phase 136.7 (cross-instance reply integrity): a reply must name its parent's author so the reply both carries the parent author in its to audience and is delivered to the parent's home instance.
Phase 136.8 (cross-instance boost integrity): a boost (Announce) of a remote object must be delivered to the object's author (the object's home) so the boost is counted on the object's home, and the object's author is named in the boost's to audience.
Best-effort: a local miss with no remote fetcher, or a remote fetch that yields no owner, returns (the caller then degrades to the prior behavior — the object's author is simply not added to the audience / not an explicit delivery recipient). The fetch is best-effort and must never fail the publish.
member.param: The persistence provider (for the local object-store lookup).
The outbound object fetcher used to resolve a remote object's owner (Phase 136.7 / 136.8); disables remote-owner resolution (local objects only).
The IRI of the object (a reply's parent, or an Announce's announced object).
A cancellation token.
member.returns: The object's owner (author) IRI, or when not resolvable.

member.summary: Computes the cross-post targets of an outbound published to a local actor's outbox (138.10 / decision 058): the REMOTE recipients the author explicitly addressed in the activity's to audience, minus the recipients the follower fan-out already covers.
member.remarks: A community *follow* is a pull (decision 036 / Phase 89.1): the follower subscribes to the followed side's content; it does not push the follower's own posts into the followed community. For an Iris-authored post to land *inside* a peered non-Iris community's post list (a Lemmy community, e.g.), the author must cross-post: explicitly address the target community in the Create's to audience and deliver the Create to that community's inbox, exactly as a Lemmy/Mastodon client cross-posts. This method reads the composed to audience (preserved by , which only appends to cc and to a reply's to) and returns the subset that is (a) remote (hosted on a different instance — a recipient on this instance's own host needs no cross-instance hop), (b) not the public-audience sentinel, (c) not already fanned out to a follower (no duplicate delivery), and (d) not blocked (the trust boundary). The result is delivered by the caller via DeliverToActorAsync (which resolves the recipient's sharedInbox/inbox and signs as the acting local actor).

The "remote" test is host-based, not actor-store-membership-based: a remote community that this instance has followed (and therefore cached in its own actor store — the peered-Lemmy case) must still be a cross-post target, because it lives on the remote host. The store membership check () would misclassify such a cached remote as local and drop the cross-post entirely; the host comparison against is the authoritative "is this on my instance" signal.
member.param: The persistence provider (provides the moderation store for the block check).

member.remarks: Docker-only-routable IRI normalization. The authoring client dials the instance on a host-published base (e.g. http://localhost:8081) and carries that base in the activity's object references (a Follow's target), but the instance stores its local actors under the advertised base (e.g. https://iris-dev1.luit.ink). Without this rewrite the local-actor check (an exact-IRI store lookup) misses the actor — the instance treats its own actor as remote and attempts a cross-instance delivery that cannot route (the dial base is not reachable from inside the instance's network). The rewrite is a no-op when the object is already on the advertised base, is not a local-actor/local-community path, or the actor/community is not local. Only the first object reference is normalized (a person/community Follow/Block/ Flag carries exactly one target).

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.ObjectLikesAsync(Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext,System.String,Iris.Server.Stores.IPersistenceProvider,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Serves the activities issued against a content object as the per-object likes collection for GET /ap/v1/{**path}/likes (the per-object like counter — decision 056 (d)). The items are the actual Like activities (each with its minted id, its actor — the liker — and its object — the liked object) — the spec-compliant, federation-friendly shape — so a client reads a like's actor off item.actor and can undo it by referencing item.id, exactly as ActivityPub's Liked relationship prescribes. Unlike the paged collections, this is a full, non-paged OrderedCollection: a like set is small and bounded (unlike an outbox), so the whole set is served at once and a client can read the exact count from totalItems.
member.remarks:
Net-state squashing. The set of Like activities is derived from the object's likers reverse index () — the net like state — not a raw activity log. A Like followed by an Undo (an unlike) removes the edge, so the undone Like is not served; a Like → Undo → Like re-adds it, so the Like is served exactly once. The collection therefore reflects only the likes that currently stand (one per liker), which is what the like count and the isLiked extension read.
likes is an extension collection, not a core ActivityStreams Object property (the only core object collection is replies). It is exposed under the bare, non-namespaced term likes — the ecosystem convention for an object-side interaction collection — so an ecosystem client that knows the term can read it uniformly for local and external objects. Per the ActivityStreams extensibility rule a strict consumer that does not know the term MUST ignore it (not error), so the bare term is safe. An object this instance does not store 404s (mirroring the object document). A liker whose Like activity was never durably stored (e.g. recorded only as an edge by an older build) degrades to a to the liker rather than being dropped, so the count stays exact.

member.summary: Drops the cached page-1 entry for any of an owner's local collection pages in the local collection-page response cache, so the next non-?refresh read re-renders with the collection's current contents.
member.remarks: Every local collection page (outbox, blocks, flags, mutes, followers, following, liked, relays, …) is served through the (a 60s-TTL server→client response cache). Any local write that mutates a collection — an outbox publish, a moderation edge (block/flag/mute), or an undo of one — must be paired with an invalidation of that collection's page-1 entry. Without it the next non-?refresh read within the TTL returns the stale page: the owner's card would not reflect the edge it just recorded (or removed) until the TTL lapses or a ?refresh=true bypass is issued. The page-1 key is the bare collection IRI ({owner}/{collection}); a change always lands in page 1's contents (an insert at the head, or a removal that shrinks the set), so invalidating page 1 is sufficient for the primary read. Deeper pages self-heal within the short TTL. Generalized from , which is now a thin alias for the outbox name.
member.param: The local collection-page response cache.
The owning actor's or community's IRI.
The collection's name segment (e.g. outbox, blocks).

member.summary: Serves an actor's followed feed (home timeline, F-14) as a paged collection for GET /ap/v1/u/{handle}/feed. The feed is the union of the actor's local and remote follows' outbox items (newest first, de-duplicated, capped by ), computed by the . Page 1 is an OrderedCollection (with first); page N > 1 is an OrderedCollectionPage (with partOf/prev /next), paged via ?page/?limit. Unlike the local collections, the feed is not served through the local collection-page response cache (it merges remote follows' outboxes over the wire on every request), but it still carries the collection Cache-Control so intermediates may cache briefly. An unknown actor 404s.

Serves the instance's public feed (the union of all local actors' outbox activities, newest first, de-duplicated, capped) as a paged collection for GET /ap/v1/public/feed. Any visitor (signed in or out) can browse this feed. Page 1 is an OrderedCollection (with first); page N > 1 is an OrderedCollectionPage (with partOf/prev /next), paged via ?page/?limit. The feed is not served through the local collection-page response cache (it re-reads all outboxes on every request), but it still carries the collection Cache-Control so intermediates may cache briefly.

member.summary: Serves the community (the library's Group actor) document for GET /ap/v1/c/{name}. The community is addressed by its handle (not an actor IRI), so the route uses {name}.

Shared core for the community collection endpoints (members, feed, following/followers, and the moderation collections blocks/flags/mutes): community existence check, page/limit parsing, collection-page document build, and response.
member.remarks: The response is served through the (the server → client response cache for the paged collection endpoints) and carries the collection Cache-Control header; ?refresh=true bypasses the cache for the read and emits a no-cache header (the value was just re-rendered — intermediates must not serve a stale copy). This mirrors the actor collection endpoint (, GET /u/{handle}/{collection}) and the community outbox (), so every Iris collection honors the same Cache-Control + ?refresh=true contract. A newly-recorded item (a member post in the feed, a new member, a new follow, a new moderation edge) is therefore visible within the TTL (max-age=60) and immediately with ?refresh=true.

member.summary: Serves the community's member actor IRIs as a paged collection for GET /ap/v1/c/{name}/members. Members are followers (change 221), so the collection is served from the community's followers set. Page 1 is an OrderedCollection (with first); page N > 1 is an OrderedCollectionPage (with partOf/prev/next), paged via ?page/?limit.

Serves the community's unified feed as a paged collection for GET /ap/v1/c/{name}/feed. The feed is the union of the community's local members' outbox activities (newest first), computed by the . Page 1 is an OrderedCollection (with first); page N > 1 is an OrderedCollectionPage (with partOf/prev/next), paged via ?page/?limit.
member.remarks: A ?q query filters the feed to the items whose content/name matches it, case-insensitively (F-23 — the feed endpoint's content filter). An empty/absent ?q returns the feed unfiltered. The filtered and unfiltered shapes are identical (the same paged collection), so the client's GetCommunityFeedAsync reads both identically.

member.summary: Serves the community's outbox — the activities the local community (a ) authors and publishes to its own outbox — as a paged collection for GET /ap/v1/c/{name}/outbox. This is the READ counterpart of POST /ap/v1/c/{name}/outbox (), which stores each published activity in the community's outbox (, keyed by the community IRI). The community document advertises this outbox IRI, so serving it keeps the document honest.
member.remarks: Mirrors the actor outbox collection endpoint (GET /u/{handle}/outbox) for a : page 1 is an OrderedCollection (with first); page N > 1 is an OrderedCollectionPage (with partOf/prev/next), paged via ?page/?limit, and served through the local collection-page response cache (so ?refresh=true bypasses it and emits a no-cache Cache-Control). An unknown community 404s.

member.summary: Serves a community's following or followers collection as a paged OrderedCollection (page 1) / OrderedCollectionPage (page N>1) for GET /ap/v1/c/{name}/{collection}. Mirrors the actor collection endpoint for a : a community follows (and is followed by) actors and other communities the same way a person does, so it carries the same following/followers collections.
member.remarks: following is backed by the community's follows set ( — the community "follows" the follower, Resolved Decision #36); the items are the followed actors'/communities' IRIs as Links. followers is backed by the community's followers set ( — F-24: when an actor follows a local community, the FollowActivityHandler records the follower in this set, so the collection lists the actors/communities that follow the community); the items are the follower IRIs as Links. Both were previously the community's follows set only — the followers set was absent, so followers always served the empty collection (the documented J-12 asymmetry); F-24 closes that. Pagination is the shared ?page/?limit shape (page 1 is the OrderedCollection with a self first; page N>1 an OrderedCollectionPage with partOf/prev/next). An unknown community 404s. The response carries the collection Cache-Control.

The community mute endpoint (19.5.4): a community's operator records or removes a community-scoped mute for an actor (the community hides the actor's content from its unified feed without severing the membership). The request is authenticated by Basic auth (the community's IRI is the credential seam, the same validator as the person mute endpoint and the community follow-decision endpoint). ?unmute=true removes the mute; otherwise it records it. Both are idempotent (re-muting / un-muting a non-existent mute is a no-op) and return 204; an unknown community 404s, an unparseable target 400s, and an unauthenticated request 401s.

Idempotent: re-blocking or unblocking a non-existent block is a no-op (204).

Creator-only: the actor is added to the community's followers set (members are followers — change 221) and the pending request is removed. Promotes a member to owner (POST /local/v1/c/{name}/owners/promote/{**actorIri}). Owner-only. Adds the actor's IRI to the Group's AttributedTo list (if not already present).
Demotes an owner (POST /local/v1/c/{name}/owners/demote/{**actorIri}). Owner-only. Removes the actor's IRI from the Group's AttributedTo list. Rejects if it would leave zero owners.
Deletes a community (DELETE /local/v1/c/{name}). Owner-only. Removes the community document and all its associated edges (followers, follows, blocks, flags, mutes, join requests).

member.summary: Serializes one page of a local collection to JSON-LD. The top-level document is written by hand (rather than through the ActivityStreams library's OrderedCollection/OrderedCollectionPage types) because the library serializes the items property with its one-or-multiple converter, which collapses a single-element page into a bare JSON string. That is legal one-or-many ActivityStreams but breaks clients that read items as an array — and the ActivityStreams spec defines OrderedCollection.items as a list. Writing the envelope by hand guarantees items is always a JSON array (empty included). Each item is still serialized through , so the item bytes are identical to the library output.

member.summary: Replaces the default in-memory delivery queue and dead-letter store with the persistent, file-backed implementations (Phase 16.2, production persistence): pending outbound deliveries (and dead-lettered deliveries) are journaled to disk and survive a host restart.
member.param: The service collection. Must not be null.
The path of the delivery-queue journal file (one JSON object per line). The directory must already exist; the file is created if it does not exist.
The path of the dead-letter journal file. The directory must already exist; the file is created if it does not exist.
The in-memory channel capacity (back-pressure bound). Defaults to .

member.returns: The service collection, for chaining.
member.remarks: Call this AFTER to override the in-memory defaults. A host that calls this gets at-least-once, restart-surviving delivery: a job is journaled (and flushed) to disk before it is handed to the in-memory channel, and on startup the journal is replayed into the channel. A job that was already delivered before a crash is re-delivered and deduped by its Id (C-07). Call on a clean shutdown to keep the journal from growing without bound.
member.exception: When or a path is null or empty.
When a capacity is less than or equal to 0.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.UseSharedDelivery(Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection,System.String,System.String,System.Nullable{System.TimeSpan},System.Nullable{System.TimeSpan},System.Int32)
member.summary: Registers the shared (Phase 84.6, shared-state scale-out): a single durable journal that two (or more) instances over the same origin enqueue into and consume from, so a delivery scheduled on instance A is delivered by A-or-B — not dropped.
member.param: The service collection. Must not be null.

The path of the shared delivery-queue journal file. All instances that share this queue must be configured with the same path. The directory must already exist; the file is created if it does not exist. A .lock file is created alongside it (the cross-process lock).
The path of the shared dead-letter journal file. The directory must already exist; the file is created if it does not exist.
How long a claim is exclusive before the job is reclaimable by another instance. Defaults to (10 min).
How long a Claimed record is retained before it is purged from the journal. Defaults to (24 h).
The dead-letter store's bounded view capacity (newest-first). Defaults to .
member.returns: The service collection, for chaining.
member.remarks: Call this AFTER to override the in-memory default. This is the scale-out counterpart to : the file-backed queue is per-instance (each instance replays its own channel), whereas the shared queue is a single journal with a visibility-timeout claim protocol (a job claimed by a live instance is not re-claimed within the visibility window; a crashed claimer's job is reclaimable). The delivery guarantee is at-least-once (a successfully-delivered job may be re-delivered when its visibility window lapses; the receiver dedupes by its Id, C-07). Use this when running two or more instances over the same origin (see the 84.5 single-instance guard, which this scale-out path is the convergence half of).
member.exception: When or a path is null or empty.
When a capacity is less than or equal to 0 or a horizon is invalid.

The channel registers the hosted service (the poller that applies events to the local RemoteActorCache + LocalActorDocumentCache); the poll interval is (default 5 s). Use this when running two or more instances over the same origin (see the 84.5 single-instance guard, which this scale-out path is the convergence half of, alongside the shared delivery queue + the document-derived key provider).

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerExtensions.NegotiateContentType(Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext)
member.summary: Negotiates the response content type. Always returns application/activity+json (F-31, spec-valid, unconditionally accepted).
member.remarks: Historically this returned application/ld+json when the client's Accept named it. That broke key resolution on some Mastodon instances (v4.6.x): their ActivityPub::FetchRemoteKeyService → fetch_resource only treats a response as a valid ActivityPub document when the content type is application/activity+json OR application/ld+json with the profile="https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams" parameter. A bare application/ld+json (no profile) fails that check, so the key fetch returns nil and the inbound request is rejected with 401 ("Unable to fetch key JSON at …#key-1"). Mastodon's own outbound build_request sends Accept: application/activity+json, application/ld+json, so this path was reachable. We therefore always emit the unambiguous application/activity+json (we still ACCEPT application/ld+json inbound for leniency — we just never emit bare ld+json).

member.summary: The IRI of the local actor the instance signs outbound federation requests as (actor-document fetches for inbound signature validation, and Phase 4 activity delivery). Defaults to the instance's first registered actor when not set. See Resolved Decision #27.

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptions.InstanceActorIri
member.summary: The IRI of the local actor whose public document is served at the instance root (GET /). Some peers (notably Lemmy) dereference the site actor from the instance's root URL before resolving any object on the instance and require that document to be an Application-type actor (the ActivityPub site-actor convention, as Mastodon/Pleroma/Friendica follow it). When set, the root serves the actor at this IRI (typically a dedicated Application whose IRI is the bare instance base) rather than the signing actor at . When null (the default), the root falls back to serving — the pre-138.11 behavior.

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptions.SharedInboxIri
member.summary: The IRI of this instance's shared inbox: a single collection that accepts activity for every local actor and community (the ActivityPub endpoints.sharedInbox property). When set, it is advertised on the public actor and community documents so remote instances may deliver to it instead of each recipient's own inbox (F-01). When not set, local documents advertise no endpoints and remote senders fall back to the per-actor inbox (the ActivityPub convention). Outbound delivery to a remote actor always honors the remote actor's own advertised sharedInbox (resolved from its document), independent of this option.

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptions.ProxySettings
member.summary: The proxy-fallback settings (Phase 6) for the POST /ap/v1/proxy/{target} endpoint: the target allowlist and the per-actor rate limit. When null, the defaults apply: an empty allowlist (every target is allowed) and requests per actor per minute.

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptions.Media
member.summary: The media-proxy (Phase 20.4 (d)) settings: the eager-warm toggle. When null, the default applies: eager-warm ON (a stored object's cross-origin attachments are pre-fetched when it is stored, so the media proxy serves them instantly).

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptions.InstanceLockPath
member.summary: The path of the single-instance lock file (Phase 84.5): when set, the host acquires a cross-process lock on startup and fails fast if a live different instance already holds it. Only one Iris instance per persistence is supported (the in-memory + file-backed providers are not safe for two processes, and even the shared EF provider leaves the actor→key binding map + delivery queue divergent), so this guard converts a silent second-instance divergence into an actionable startup error. When null (the default), the guard is inert (no lock, no check) — the common single-process deployment and the multi-host test harnesses are unaffected.

Defaults to 30 s. A non-positive value disables the periodic refresh (the startup convergence pass still runs). The service is inert when the instance's IKeyProvider is not a (the single-instance default), so this interval has no effect on the common single-process deployment.

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptions.ObjectInteractionRefreshInterval
member.summary: How often the object-interaction-count refresh hosted service (Phase 151 — background processing) re-computes the per-object interaction counters (iris:likedCount/sharedCount/repliedCount/dislikedCount/score) and persists them onto the stored object documents: a like/boost/reply/dislike recorded on this instance becomes visible on the object document (and in collection pages) within one interval, so reads can serve the pre-computed counters instead of walking the reverse indexes on every read. member.name: T:Iris.Server.MediaOptions
member.summary: Settings for the media proxy (Phase 20.4 (d), browser-loadable external media).
member.remarks: The media proxy fetches an external attachment url on demand (lazy-by-nature: warmed on the first proxy hit). member.name: T:Iris.Server.ProxySettings
member.summary: Settings for the proxy-fallback endpoint (POST /ap/v1/proxy/{target}, Phase 6).
member.remarks: The proxy signs an authenticated actor's requests with that actor's own key and forwards them to an arbitrary target, so it is a powerful capability and is bounded by two independent policies: a target allowlist (which hosts may be proxied) and a per-actor rate limit (how often a given actor may use the proxy). Both default to permissive (empty allowlist = all targets allowed; /minute) so a host that does not configure gets a working proxy out of the box, and a production host tightens the allowlist.

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ProxySettings.AllowedHosts

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ProxySettings.MaxRequestsPerMinute
member.summary: The maximum number of proxy requests a single actor may issue per minute. Defaults to .

member.name: P:Iris.Server.ProxySettings.AllowAnonymousReads
member.summary: Whether the anonymous proxy seam (GET /ap/v1/proxy/{target}) is enabled. When enabled, a signed-out visitor's browser may read public remote content (an actor document, an object) through the same-origin proxy instead of dialing the remote instance directly — a direct cross-origin GET is CORS-blocked (or CSP-blocked) in the browser, so the signed-out UI otherwise cannot render remote actors' avatars or profiles. The seam relays ONLY GET reads, applies the same target allowlist as the authenticated proxy, and is bounded by its own per-IP rate limit (it has no actor identity). Defaults to ; a host that does not want anonymous cross-instance reads sets it (anonymous reads then 404 and the UI falls back to a direct fetch).

member.name: T:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptionsValidator
member.summary: Startup validation for : makes a misconfigured production deployment fail fast with an actionable error (at host start) instead of surfacing later as a runtime 500 or a silently-misrouted federation request.
member.remarks:
Validated invariants (Phase 83.2):
— when set, must be an absolute http(s) IRI (it is used to build absolute IRIs for local actors and in WebFinger; a relative or non-http(s) base would produce malformed actor IRIs that no remote instance can fetch).
— when set, must be an absolute http(s) IRI (it is the actor the instance signs outbound federation as; a malformed IRI would break every outbound request's signature).
— when set, must be an absolute http(s) IRI (it names the actor whose public document the instance root serves; a malformed IRI would 404 the site-actor dereference that peers such as Lemmy perform before resolving any object).
— when set, must be an absolute http(s) IRI (it is advertised as the shared-inbox endpoint; a malformed IRI would reject every inbound delivery).
Null is allowed for every option (a host may configure a subset); validation only fires when a value is present and is malformed. This keeps the validator non-breaking for hosts that rely on the defaults or configure only some options.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.ActivityPubServerOptionsValidator.IsValidHttpIri(Iris.Core.Identity.Iri)
member.summary: An IRI is a valid federation base/actor/inbox IRI when it is absolute and uses the http or https scheme (the only schemes a remote instance can fetch). A fragment is permitted (an actor IRI may carry one); the scheme + absoluteness are the invariants that matter here.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.AnnounceIris
member.summary: Shared helpers for the Announce (boost/repost) lifecycle: the activity a local actor uses to propagate a boost to a follower. (Resolving an object IRI from an lives in .)
member.remarks: An Announce is a local actor re-sharing an object (a boost/repost). When the local actor's followers live on other instances, the local instance must propagate the Announce to each local follower's inbox so the follower's client can display the boosted content.
member.para: Id model (decision 055, "mint once at record-time, reuse for all deliveries"). The boost's id is minted once — by the outbox write path (an unguessable ULID) or, for an inbound boost, taken verbatim from the remote originator — and every propagated copy to each follower reuses that same id (only the per-follower to/cc addressing differs). Reusing one id keeps the activity idempotent: the same boost delivered to two followers — or redelivered on retry — is the same activity, so a follower that stores by IRI does not accumulate duplicates. The announcer's own outbox keeps the original announce (the same id), so the boost is discoverable from the announcer's outbox and from each follower's inbox.
The propagated Announce is addressed directly to each local follower (to = the follower's actor IRI, cc = the announcer's actor IRI) and carries the original announce's id.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Bootstrap.SingleInstanceGuardHostedService
member.summary: A hosted service that acquires the at startup and releases it at shutdown (Phase 84.5; lifted in Phase 84.6 to support multi-instance scale-out).
member.remarks:
When is configured, this service is registered by AddActivityPubServer. On it calls : a lock held by a live different instance is a collision. The guard's behavior on a collision depends on whether the scale-out convergence pieces are all configured (Phase 84.6):
All three configured (the as IKeyProvider + the as IDeliveryQueue + the as ICacheInvalidationPublisher): multi-instance is supported — the instances converge via the shared state (the document-derived key provider re-derives keys from the durable documents; the shared delivery queue is a single journal; the cache-invalidation channel propagates actor-document changes). The guard logs a warning and does not fail host startup (the operator is informed, but the deployment is valid).
Any missing: multi-instance is unsafe (the instances would diverge on the un-converged surface — the actor→key binding map, the delivery queue, or the actor/edge caches). The guard fails fast (throws ), and the operator must either stop the other instance, point this instance at a different persistence, or configure the missing scale-out piece(s).
On it disposes the lock (deletes the lock file). When no lock path is configured (the default — every test harness and the in-memory/file-backed deployments), this service is not registered and the guard is inert: existing multi-host test setups and single-process deployments are unaffected.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Bootstrap.SingleInstanceLock
member.summary: A cross-process single-instance lock that guards a shared persistence against a second, concurrent Iris instance (Phase 84.5).

remarks.para: Phase 84's survey of the per-process state surfaces found that two Iris instances sharing one persistence would silently diverge on every in-process surface — most dangerously the actor→key binding map (a rotation on instance A is invisible to B's signer) and the in-memory delivery queue (a delivery queued on A is never sent by B). The in-memory and file-backed implementations are not safe for two processes at all (each holds its own in-memory copy of the whole graph); only the EF/Postgres provider shares state, and even it leaves the binding map + delivery queue divergent. There was no guard against this: a second instance on the same persistence simply started and diverged.

The lock is held for the owning process's lifetime: the OS releases the handle on normal exit ( deletes the file) and on a crash (the handle is closed, so a new instance can steal it via the liveness check). No advisory-lock P/Invoke is required — the lock file + PID liveness is portable across the platforms Iris targets. A recycled PID (the prior owner's id reassigned to an unrelated process before a new instance starts) would be misread as "alive"; that window is vanishingly small, and its consequence is only a (safe) failed startup that the operator resolves by deleting the stale lock file.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Caching.CacheInvalidationChannel
member.summary: A file-backed, cross-process cache-invalidation channel (Phase 84.6, shared-state scale-out): two (or more) Iris instances over the same origin share one durable invalidation journal, so an actor-document change on instance A invalidates the in-memory actor/edge caches on instance B without a restart or a cache TTL expiry.
member.remarks: The single-instance gap. The in-memory actor/edge caches (, ) are per-instance: each instance holds its own . When instance A updates a local actor (a key rotation re-stamping the actor document's publicKey, a profile change, etc.), instance B's cached copy of that actor's document is now stale — B serves the old document (and resolves the old key from it) for up to the cache's TTL (1 hour for the remote-actor cache). The 84.5 single-instance guard made the single-instance constraint explicit; this channel is the scale-out half: a shared invalidation journal two instances can coexist over.

Model: an append-only invalidation journal over a JSON file. Each journaled line is a — a monotonic Seq (event position), the affected ActorIri, and a At timestamp (UTC). The journal is guarded by a cross-process file lock (a separate .lock file opened exclusively); every read-modify-write (a publish, a purge) holds that lock so two instances never interleave a journal edit.
appends an event with the next Seq.
returns the events with Seq > sinceSeq (the new events since the reader's last cursor), in order. A reader's cursor is its own in-memory state (the channel does not track per-reader cursors — each reader passes its own sinceSeq).
Events older than the retention window are purged (removed from the journal) so the file does not grow without bound. A reader that has not polled since a purge simply re-reads the retained events (a late reader re-invalidates a cache that was already invalidated — a harmless no-op).

Delivery guarantee: at-least-once. An event is journaled (and flushed) before returns, so a crash after the flush leaves it for replay. A reader that polls and then crashes (before applying the invalidation) re-reads the same events on its next poll and re-applies the invalidation — a harmless no-op (invalidating an already-invalidated cache entry is a no-op). The journal is bounded by the retention window (default 1 hour), so a reader that is down longer than the retention window misses events — but after an hour the cache entries are stale enough that a TTL expiry (or a manual invalidation) is the expected recovery path, not the channel.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Caching.CacheInvalidationService
member.summary: A hosted service that applies cross-instance cache-invalidation events to the local actor/edge caches on a fixed interval (Phase 84.6, shared-state scale-out — the "when" of the invalidation).

remarks.para: The is the channel: a shared, file-backed invalidation journal two (or more) instances over the same origin publish to and poll from. This service is the reader: on host start, and then every (default 5 s; a non-positive value disables the periodic poll but still runs the startup pass), it polls the channel for new events (since its last-seen Seq cursor) and, for each event, invalidates the local + entries for the affected actor IRI.

The service is registered only when a is registered (via UseCacheInvalidationChannel); with the single-instance default (no channel) the service is not registered, so the common single-instance deployment and every existing test harness are unaffected.

The poll is best-effort: a failed read (a transient I/O blip) is logged and the next tick retries; it never throws into the host. The cursor (lastSeq) is in-memory (a restart re-reads the journal from Seq 0, which is a harmless re-invalidating no-op for already-invalidated entries).

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Caching.ILocalActorResolver
member.summary: Resolves whether a given actor IRI is a local actor (one hosted by this instance, in the instance's ).
member.remarks: Inbound activity handlers use this to decide how to interpret an activity. The records a follow edge only when the recipient is a local actor (a remote recipient's follow is not this instance's concern); the and finalize or undo the follow state only when the follower is a local actor (the local actor's own follow, which it sent and now accepts or rejects). A remote follower's accept/reject is a no-op here: the remote instance owns that follow's state.

member.summary: Caches the rendered **local** collection documents (an actor's outbox, followers, and following — served from persistence) by the page's IRI. member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.DeliveryCircuitBreakerOptions
member.summary: Options for the per-peer outbound-delivery circuit breaker (Phase 17.3, production scaling).
member.remarks: When a peer's inbox endpoint is down (repeatedly returning 5xx / timing out), the worker would otherwise retry every queued job to that peer with its full budget — hammering a downed peer with a stream of doomed requests while the queue backs up. A circuit breaker stops this: once a peer accumulates consecutive failures, the circuit for that peer opens and deliveries to that peer are skipped (dead-lettered immediately, not retried) for . After the open duration elapses, the circuit enters the half-open state: a single probe delivery is allowed through. If the probe succeeds the circuit closes (the peer is healthy again); if it fails the circuit re-opens for another .

Peer key. The breaker keys on the host of the recipient's inbox IRI (e.g. https://b.domain.local/ap/v1/u/bob/inbox → b.domain.local), mirroring the : all of a peer's inboxes (shared inbox + per-actor inboxes) share a single circuit.

Disabled. A of 0 (the default) disables the breaker entirely — the worker delivers exactly as before (per-job retry + dead-letter, no per-peer circuit). A host opts in by rebinding this to a positive threshold.

member.name: P:Iris.Server.Delivery.DeliveryCircuitBreakerOptions.FailureThreshold
member.summary: The number of consecutive failures (across all deliveries to a peer) that opens the circuit for that peer. Must be at least 0 (0 = circuit breaker disabled, the default; the worker delivers with per-job retry only). Defaults to 0.

member.name: P:Iris.Server.Delivery.DeliveryCircuitBreakerOptions.OpenDuration
member.summary: How long the circuit stays open (deliveries to the peer are skipped) before it transitions to half-open (a single probe is allowed). Must be positive when is greater than 0. Defaults to 60 seconds.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.DeliveryRateLimitOptions
member.summary: Options for the per-peer outbound-delivery rate limit (Phase 16.3, production scaling).
member.remarks: A production instance delivering a burst of activities (a relay fan-out, a popular actor posting to many followers, or a retry storm to a downed peer) can overwhelm a single remote peer's inbox endpoint. bounds how many deliveries the worker may send to a single peer (keyed by the host of the recipient's inbox IRI) per sliding minute. A value of 0 (the default) disables the rate limit entirely — the worker delivers as fast as the concurrency cap allows.

Why per host, not per inbox IRI. A well-behaved instance wants a single outbound rate to a remote peer (its host), not one per inbox: a peer's shared inbox and its per-actor inboxes all live on the same host, and spreading deliveries across inboxes would let the instance exceed the peer's comfortable intake rate. The rate limit is therefore keyed by the inbox IRI's host. This complements the Phase 16.1 concurrency cap: bounds how many deliveries are in flight at once (connection-pool pressure), while this bounds how fast the worker may send to a given peer over time (peer politeness).

member.name: P:Iris.Server.Delivery.DeliveryRateLimitOptions.PerPeerMaxRequestsPerMinute
member.summary: The maximum number of deliveries the worker may send to a single peer (keyed by the host of the recipient's inbox IRI) per sliding minute. Must be at least 0 (0 = rate limiting disabled, the default; the worker delivers as fast as the concurrency cap allows). Defaults to 0.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.DeliveryRetryOptions
member.summary: Options for the retry / dead-letter policy (F-22 at-least-once delivery).
member.remarks: A delivery that fails (network error or a non-2xx response) is retried up to total attempts (the initial attempt + − 1 retries). Between attempts the worker waits an exponentially-growing delay ( doubled each retry, capped at ) so a downed peer is not hammered. When all attempts fail, the job is moved to the dead-letter store (an operator can inspect and re-drive it) rather than dropped silently. A host may rebind this to tune the retry budget (e.g. a higher for a lossy network, or = 1 for fail-fast).
member.para: Note on "at-least-once": a delivery that succeeds but whose acknowledgement is lost (the POST returned 2xx but the response was dropped) is not detected — the worker treats a 2xx as delivered. The retry policy therefore gives *at-least-once for failed attempts* (a delivery is never dropped before tries) but not idempotent exactly-once; the receiving instance's inbox pipeline dedupes a re-delivered activity by its Id (C-07), so a retried delivery is harmless (it is a no-op on the receiver).

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.DeliveryWorker
member.summary: The background worker that pumps s off the and delivers them — POSTing the serialized activity to the recipient's inbox, signed with the instance actor's key.
member.remarks: The worker is a (per the async conventions — background delivery uses a Channel + hosted service, never Task.Run). It dequeues jobs until the queue is complete and empty (signaled by , called on host shutdown), then stops.

Concurrency (Phase 16.1): the worker delivers jobs with bounded concurrency — at most deliveries in flight at once (a semaphore admits one slot per delivery; a delivery releases its slot when it finishes). A value of 1 (the default) preserves the original serial behavior; a higher value delivers a burst in parallel, overlapping the per-delivery network round-trips, without opening more than that many concurrent outbound connections. The dequeuer pulls a job and starts its delivery task outside the in-flight bound, so a slow delivery can never stall the pump (which would serialize the worker and risk a semaphore deadlock). Each in-flight delivery still honors the per-job retry / dead-letter policy independently.

Signing: each delivery is signed as the local actor named on its (the actor performing the automated event — e.g. the local actor being followed in a Follow → Accept). When a job carries no acting actor, the worker falls back to — the "system key for automated events". The acting actor is communicated to the via the X-Iris-Actor request header (which the handler treats as a per-request override of its default ); the handler resolves that actor's key from the .

Failure policy (F-22 at-least-once delivery): a delivery that fails (network error or a non-2xx response) is retried up to total attempts, with an exponentially-growing backoff between attempts ( doubled each retry, capped at ) so a downed peer is not hammered. When all attempts fail, the job is moved to the (an operator can inspect and re-drive it) rather than dropped silently. A successful (2xx) delivery is never retried. A retried delivery is harmless on the receiver: the inbox pipeline dedupes a re-delivered activity by its Id (C-07). This follows the error-handling convention (log, don't throw) — a delivery failure never crashes the worker.

Retry hardening (Phase 17.3): a 4xx response (other than 429) is treated as permanent — the job is dead-lettered immediately without exhausting the retry budget (a bad inbox or auth failure will not succeed on retry). A Retry-After response header (429/503) is honored: when the server tells the worker how long to wait before retrying, the worker uses that delay (in place of the exponential backoff) when it is longer.

Circuit breaker (Phase 17.3): when a per-peer is configured, the worker checks it before each delivery. If the circuit for the job's inbox host is open (the peer has accumulated too many consecutive failures), the delivery is skipped and the job is dead-lettered immediately (without a network call) — this stops the worker from hammering a downed peer with a stream of doomed requests. Successful deliveries reset the peer's failure count; failed deliveries increment it. When the count reaches the threshold the circuit opens for ; after that it transitions to half-open and allows a single probe (a success closes the circuit, a failure re-opens it).

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.DeliveryWorkerOptions
member.summary: Options for the outbound-delivery concurrency (Phase 16.1, production scaling).
member.remarks:
The worker pumps s off the and POSTs them to recipients' inboxes. By default it delivers them serially (one in flight at a time), which is simple but leaves a production instance's outbound bandwidth idle when a burst of deliveries is queued (a popular local actor posting, a community following many remote actors, a relay fan-out).
bounds how many deliveries may be in flight at once. A value greater than 1 lets the worker deliver a burst in parallel — overlapping the per-delivery network round-trips — while still capping the number of concurrent outbound connections the instance opens (so a burst cannot exhaust the local connection pool or hammer a single remote peer). The value is a concurrency cap, not a rate limit: deliveries are not throttled in time, only bounded in parallelism. Each in-flight delivery still honors the per-job retry / dead-letter policy independently.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.FileBackedDeliveryDeadLetterStore
member.summary: A persistent, file-backed (Phase 16.2, production persistence): dead-lettered deliveries are journaled to disk (one JSON object per line) so they survive a restart and an operator can still inspect — and re-drive — permanently-failed deliveries after the process restarts.
member.remarks: The default is ephemeral — a host restart loses the dead-letter history (the operator can no longer see which deliveries permanently failed). A production instance wants that history to survive a restart. This store keeps the same in-memory bounded, newest-first view as the in-memory store (so the and any operator tooling see identical behavior) and additionally journals each recorded entry to a file. On construction it re-reads the file to restore the entries that were held when the previous process stopped.

Bounding and eviction. The in-memory view holds at most capacity entries (the most recent; the oldest are evicted). The journal file, however, is append-only and is not trimmed on eviction (eviction is an in-memory view concern, not a durability concern — the file is the operator's full dead-letter log). A production host that wants a bounded file would pair this with a periodic rotation (out of scope here); for a bounded run the file grows with the number of dead-lettered deliveries.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.FileBackedDeliveryQueue
member.summary: A persistent, file-backed (Phase 16.2, production persistence): pending outbound federation s are journaled to disk (one JSON object per line) as they are enqueued, and replayed into an in-memory channel on construction.
member.remarks: The default is ephemeral — a host restart loses every pending delivery (a follow that was scheduled to be delivered, a boost, a relay fan-out). A production instance wants those to survive a restart so the federation edge is not silently dropped. This queue journals each enqueued job to a file (append, line-delimited) before it is handed to the in-memory channel, and on construction re-reads the file to replay any jobs that were pending when the previous process stopped.

Durability model. Enqueueing is at-least-once: a job is journaled to disk (and flushed) before it is written to the channel, so a crash after the flush leaves the job on disk for replay; a crash before the flush loses the job (the same window as the in-memory queue). The receiving instance dedupes a re-delivered activity by its Id (C-07), so replaying a job that was in fact already delivered is a harmless no-op. The in-memory channel provides the same back pressure and bounded capacity as .

Replay and truncation. On construction, existing journal lines are parsed and enqueued into the channel. A job that was already dequeued by the previous process (and is now being redelivered) is harmless (deduped by the receiver). To prevent the journal from growing without bound across many restarts (jobs that were replayed and delivered but never removed from the file), rewrites the journal to contain only the jobs still pending — call it on a clean shutdown (after the queue has drained) to keep the file small. When is not called, the journal is append-only and grows with every delivery (acceptable for a bounded run; a production host should truncate on clean shutdown).

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.IDeletePropagationService
member.summary: Propagates an object or to the remote actors that need to see it (the federated write half of F-02/F-03).
member.remarks: When a local actor edits or deletes an object this instance stores, the change is not enough to land in the local (the / do that): the actors on other instances that saw the object must be told, or their copies go stale (a remote instance keeps serving the pre-edit content, or the pre-delete content in place of a ). This service is the single owner of that fan-out: it computes the propagation target set from the object's , the local , and the local , and schedules the activity for delivery to each remote target via (signed as the local author).
member.para:
Target computation. For an object owned by local actor A, the targets are:
A's remote followers (the actors who saw the object via 's outbound Create federation, Slice 11.7) — they need the refreshed / tombstoned content to keep their copy consistent.
The object's attributedTo (the author) when the author is remote — a post published to a remote author's outbox (a Create addressed to them) is theirs, so they need to know it was edited or deleted (they serve it by IRI from their object store).
The object's parents (the objects it replies to) when a parent is owned by a remote actor — the parent's instance holds the parent object's replies collection (F-12); when a reply is deleted, that parent's replies edge is removed there. (When the parent is local the edge is removed locally by the handler; a remote parent cannot be told to drop an edge it does not index per-object, so only the parent's owner is targeted and the edge removal on this instance is local-only.)
Targets that are local actors are skipped: a local actor's copy is on this instance and is refreshed / tombstoned locally by the handler (no cross-instance delivery).

Determinism. The propagation activity's Id is derived from the object IRI ({objectIri}/updates/{guid-N} / {objectIri}/deletes/{guid-N}) so a re-delivered propagation is deduplicated by the receiving instance's inbox pipeline (C-07).

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Delivery.IDeliveryCircuitBreaker
member.summary: A per-peer outbound-delivery circuit breaker (Phase 17.3, production scaling): stops the from hammering a downed peer. When a peer's inbox endpoint accumulates enough consecutive failures, the circuit for that peer opens and deliveries to that peer are skipped (dead-lettered immediately, not retried) until the peer recovers.
member.remarks: The peer is keyed by the host of the recipient's inbox IRI (e.g. https://b.domain.local/ap/v1/u/bob/inbox → b.domain.local), mirroring the : all of a peer's inboxes share a single circuit.

States. Each peer's circuit is in one of three states:
ClosedNormal operation. Deliveries are allowed; consecutive failures are counted.
OpenThe peer has failed enough times. Deliveries to the peer are skipped (the worker dead-letters them immediately without a network call) until OpenDuration elapses.
Half-openThe open duration has elapsed. A single probe delivery is allowed through. If it succeeds the circuit closes; if it fails the circuit re-opens.
