member.name: M:Iris.Server.Services.FeedService.TruncateDedup(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{KristofferStrube.ActivityStreams.IObjectOrLink})
member.summary: De-duplicates the merged items and truncates to .
member.remarks:
Two de-dup passes, applied in order, then the cap:
By item IRI — keep the first occurrence of each activity IRI (a cross-post scenario where the same activity IRI appears in two follows' outboxes).
By content object — a single object can surface in the feed under more than one activity type: an actor's own Create of a note, and a follower's Announce (boost) of the same note, are two distinct activities with two distinct IRIs but one piece of content. Left un-coalesced the home timeline renders the note twice (once as the author's post, once as the boost). Items are grouped by the IRI of the object a Create/Announce references; per group a single representative is kept — an item carrying the object embedded (rich, renderable without an extra fetch) is preferred over a link-only reference, so the author's content-bearing Create wins over a booster's bare Announce. Non-content items (plain objects, and social activities such as Like/Follow) are never coalesced.
The cap () is applied last, so a duplicate consuming a slot does not displace a legitimate item. Items without an IRI are kept (they cannot be de-duplicated).

the outboxes of the actor's local follows (read from the local activity store — no network), and

member.remarks: The per-actor feed cache (, 30 s TTL) merges the actor's current following set. When a follow edge the actor depends on changes — most importantly an un-follow (an Undo of a Follow) — the cached feed still contains the (now-unfollowed) actor's posts until the TTL lapses. Without this invalidation, an un-follower "still sees messages from an unfollowed user" for up to the cache TTL (and longer if the client honors the feed's Cache-Control). Callers invoke this at the follow-edge write sites (the outbox Follow/Undo branches and the inbound handlers that record/remove a local edge). The default implementation is a no-op, so an implementation without a server-side cache (or a test double) need not override it.

member.summary: Searches an instance's own (local) actors and content objects (F-13 global search / directory).
member.remarks: The gap (F-13): only per-community search (GET /c/{name}/search) exists — a user cannot discover actors or content instance-wide. This service is the instance-wide counterpart: it searches the local surface this instance stores — the actors it hosts (its directory) and the content objects it has stored (via the inbound Create path, including copies federated in from remote authors) — so the server can serve a GET /search endpoint.

Search surface. A query matches:
a local actor (its name, preferredUsername, or IRI), and
a stored content object (its content or name), skipping s (a deleted object has no searchable content) and objects that are actors (those are matched by the actor pass, not duplicated as content).
Matching is a case-insensitive substring over the relevant string fields (the same shape as the community search, ). An empty/whitespace query matches all actors and content objects (the endpoint then serves as an unfiltered directory / listing).

Ordering. Results are deterministic: actors first, then content objects, each sub-list sorted by IRI (ordinal). The endpoint slices the combined list into pages (the shared limit/offset pagination shape).

Scope. This searches the instance's own store only. It does not query remote instances (a cross-instance search would require a relay / WebFinger fan-out, which is out of scope for F-13 — it matches the per-community search, which also searches only the local surface).

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Services.VisibilityFilter
member.summary: The audience/visibility predicate for the instance's read surfaces (public feed, global search, and — later — the follow feed and object-document endpoints). Iris models visibility purely with the ActivityStreams to/cc audience, the same convention the platform uses for delivery; there is no first-class "visibility" column. This helper centralizes the single rule every read surface must apply so a non-public (followers-only or direct) post is not surfaced to users who are not an intended recipient.
member.remarks:
The rule (matching Mastodon / ActivityPub convention):
A post is public when its to/cc contains the public-audience sentinel (as:Public), or when it has no named audience at all (a note with no to/cc is public by convention — the codebase's existing IsFollowReply heuristic relies on the same "no audience ⇒ public" rule).
A post that names an audience but is not public (followers-only or a direct message) is visible only to a requester who is one of its named recipients (appears in to/cc).
Feed items are s (a Create/Announce) whose audience lives on the embedded content object, so extracts the embedded object (or the item itself, when it is a bare object) and applies the rule to it.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.Services.VisibilityFilter.IsVisibleTo(KristofferStrube.ActivityStreams.IObject,System.Nullable{Iris.Core.Identity.Iri})

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Stores.ActorCountRefreshService
member.summary: A background service that pre-computes the per-actor counters (iris:postsCount, iris:followersCount, iris:followingCount) and persists them onto the stored actor documents.

remarks.para: Before this service, the actor-document and community-document read paths computed these counters on every read by walking the actor's outbox () and the follow store ( / ) — an O(outbox + follows) sweep per actor, per request. The counters are cacheable (not per-requester), change only when a post/follow/unfollow is recorded, and the same actor is read many more times than it is interacted with.

This service inverts that: on a fixed interval ( , default 30 s; a non-positive value disables the periodic refresh but still runs the startup pass) it enumerates every stored actor (), computes the three counters, and writes them onto the actor's under the deployment's iris: namespace. The actor is then re-stored via , so the counts become durable and serveable without a per-read sweep.

The postsCount classification mirrors the read-time CountPostsAsync in : an outbox item counts as a post when it is an (boost) or a whose object is a or . Social and moderation activities (Follow, Accept, Like, Flag, …) are excluded.

The refresh is best-effort and idempotent: an actor whose stored counts already match the freshly computed values is not re-stored (no spurious write / no cache invalidation churn). A failed pass is logged and the next tick retries; it never throws into the host. The service is a no-op when the instance stores no actors.

The stored actor's privateKey extension (owner-only PEM) is preserved through the re-store: the service mutates the in-memory actor's in place and calls with the same instance, so all existing extension properties are serialized back to storage.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Stores.IAnnounceStore
member.summary: Records and queries announce (boost / re-share) relationships.
member.remarks:
An announce (boost) is the directed edge announcer → announcedObject. The store tracks both directions:
The announcer → [announced objects] direction, so the actor's boosts can be listed (mirroring the actor's liked collection for likes).
The announced object → [announcers] reverse index, so an object's shares collection (and thus its boost count) can be assembled without scanning every stored activity — the per-object interaction counter deferred by decision 056 (d).
Both directions are maintained atomically on / . The store is the durable record of a boost: the records an inbound boost here (and in the recipient's outbox), and the removes it on an Undo of the boost.

member.remarks: The store keys the item by the SHA-256 of (a server-internal dedupe index: the same bytes fetched from any source URL are stored once) and records the source URL → media-IRI mapping (the URL is the client-facing key — the client always knows the originator's attachment url, so a cold external object the content hash could not pre-cover still resolves). The content hash is never exposed to the client; the URL is the stable identifier the proxy and the eager-warm hook use.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Stores.IModerationStore
member.summary: Records and queries moderation relationships (F-07): the directed block edges blocker → blocked, flag edges flagger → flagged, and mute edges muter → muted an instance knows about.
member.remarks:
A Block activity (ActivityPub §5.2.1.3) carries actor = the blocking actor and object = the blocked actor. The store records the directed edge so:
a local actor's blocks collection (served at GET /ap/v1/u/{handle}/blocks) lists the actors it has blocked, and
the instance can determine whether an actor is blocked (e.g. to exclude a blocked actor's content from a local actor's feed, or to suppress outbound delivery to an actor that blocked a local actor).
The edge is recorded for either direction of locality: when a local actor blocks someone, or when someone blocks a local actor (so the local actor knows it is blocked). A Flag (AS2.0) is the same shape (a moderation report) and is recorded identically when either party is local. A Mute is Iris-specific (there is no ActivityStreams type): it is a local moderation decision (a local actor mutes a follow to hide its content from its feed without severing the follow, the inverse of a block's hard exclusion) recorded from a local, authenticated request — it is not interpreted from a federated activity. A production host may swap in a persistent store; the handlers and endpoints depend only on this interface.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Stores.IRelayStore
member.summary: Records and queries relay subscriptions (F-06): the directed edges subscribingActor → relay an instance's local actors have to relays (fan-out servers).
member.remarks:
A relay is a star-subscribed fan-out server (ActivityPub §5.1.3): an actor advertises the relays it subscribes to via the star actor property, and its content is delivered to those relays so the relays can fan it out to the wider federation. This store records which relays a local actor subscribes to, so:
the actor's relays collection (served at GET /ap/v1/u/{handle}/relays) and the star property on the actor document list the relays it subscribes to, and
the instance can deliver the actor's content to each subscribed relay (the relay fan-out, the follow-up slice).
A relay subscription is an Iris-specific local decision (a local actor configures the relays it wants to fan out through): it is recorded from a local, authenticated request — it is not interpreted from a federated activity (a relay is a remote server the actor points at, not an activity the actor receives). A production host may swap in a persistent store; the handlers and endpoints depend only on this interface.

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Stores.IReplyStore
member.summary: Records and queries reply (thread) relationships between content objects (F-12).
member.remarks: A reply is the directed edge childObject → parentObject (an object's inReplyTo). The store tracks, for each parent object, the objects that reply to it, so a note's replies collection (served at {object}/replies) can be assembled without scanning every stored object. The parent → [child] direction is what a thread reader needs (the replies to a note); the reverse (child → parent) is already carried by the stored object's inReplyTo and is read via .

member.name: T:Iris.Server.Stores.ObjectInteractionCountRefreshService
member.summary: A background service that pre-computes the per-object interaction counters (iris:likedCount, iris:sharedCount, iris:repliedCount, iris:dislikedCount, and iris:score) and persists them onto the stored object documents (Phase 151 — background processing).

remarks.para: Before this service, the object-document and collection-page read paths computed these counters on every read by walking the , , , and reverse indexes (an O(n) sweep per object, per request). At scale that is wasted work: the counters are cacheable (not per-requester), change only when a like/boost/reply/dislike edge is recorded or removed, and the same object is read many more times than it is interacted with.

This service inverts that: on a fixed interval ( , default 30 s; a non-positive value disables the periodic refresh but still runs the startup pass) it enumerates every stored object (), batch-reads the four reverse indexes in a single pass, and writes the resulting counts onto each non-tombstone object's under the deployment's iris: namespace. The object is then re-stored via , so the counts become durable and serveable without a per-read sweep.

The refresh is best-effort and idempotent: an object whose stored counts already match the freshly computed values is not re-stored (no spurious write / no cache invalidation churn). A failed pass (a transient persistence blip) is logged and the next tick retries; it never throws into the host. The service is a no-op when the instance stores no objects, so a host with an empty store is unaffected.

member.name: M:Iris.Server.Stores.ObjectInteractionCountRefreshService.RefreshObjectCountsAsync(Iris.Core.Identity.Iri,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Re-computes and persists the per-object interaction counters for a single stored object, so the object's denormalized likedCount / sharedCount / repliedCount / dislikedCount reflect a just-recorded (or removed) like / boost / reply / dislike edge immediately, rather than waiting for the next interval pass. No-op when the object is not stored locally (a remote object's counters live on the object's home instance), is a tombstone, has no resolvable IRI, or no iris: namespace is configured.

remarks.para: The object-document and collection-page read paths serve the pre-computed counters (persisted onto the stored object's ) when present, and only fall back to the per-read reverse-index sweep when they are absent. Once the startup / first tick has persisted a zero for an object that has no edges, a subsequent like does not make those counters absent — it leaves them stale until the next interval pass. Calling this right after recording (or removing) a like edge closes that gap: the counter is refreshed synchronously so the very next read of the object's document is correct (S37 — a remote Like is stored and the /likes collection is correct, but the Note's likedCount stays 0 until the 30 s refresh tick).

member.param: The IRI of the stored object whose counters should be refreshed.
A cancellation token.
